original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Reuse the committed SOURCES.json payload already authenticated by the complete publication byte/history check, without changing ancestry operations.
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card is narrowed to duplicate publication metadata reads; it is a tooling improvement, not a mathematical replay.
bottleneck_link: Publication preflight is required before research submission; avoiding duplicate immutable-source reads reduces that wait while preserving its evidence contract.
stop_rule: Stop at the first reproducible complete-check improvement with identical receipts and passing rejection controls; otherwise publish a bounded negative finding.
evidence: Nine alternating runs per arm on each of two real packages; all 36 complete receipts match within package. Median reductions 18.33% and 15.66%. Hash-bound controls and optional benchmark emit stdout receipts.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does the same complete-check improvement remain measurable on a second operating system and Git implementation?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The local improvement does not establish cross-host timing behavior.
open_questions.first_step: Run benchmark.py on the same two unchanged package inventories, with nine alternating samples and complete receipt equality.
open_questions.blocked_by: A second host and matching materialized fixtures.
